title: Count the Number of Complete Components
summary: Given an integer n, determine the count of fully connected subgraphs within a graph having n vertices numbered from 0 to n-1.
statement: Given an integer n, determine the count of fully connected subgraphs within a graph having n vertices numbered from 0 to n-1. Each subgraph must be fully connected, meaning every pair of vertices within it is directly connected by an edge, and no vertex in the subgraph connects to any outside vertex.
constraints: The inputs describe a simple undirected graph on vertices zero through n-1.
A connected component is complete when every pair of its vertices has an edge between them.
Return the number of complete connected components, including isolated vertices.
hints: Count its vertices and sum their graph degrees.
A size-s complete simple component has degree sum s*(s-1).
Connectivity is guaranteed by traversal, and a simple component reaches the maximum possible internal edge count exactly when every vertex pair is adjacent.
editorial: Connectivity is guaranteed by traversal, and a simple component reaches the maximum possible internal edge count exactly when every vertex pair is adjacent.

tests.explanation: The triangle, the two-vertex edge, and isolated vertex five are three complete components.
The triangle is complete but the three-node path is not, so only one component qualifies.
